questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which statement is the best focused purpose for a short speech?

answer.text: A. I will discuss several things about school.

feedback.text: This is broad and does not tell the audience the exact point of the speech.

answer.text: B. I will explain how daily practice helps speakers become more confident.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives one clear idea that can guide the whole speech.

answer.text: C. Speaking, school, and sports are interesting.

feedback.text: This lists unrelated topics instead of giving one coherent focus.

answer.text: D. My speech is about anything important.

feedback.text: This is vague. A focused speech needs a specific direction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which order best fits a speech explaining how to prepare for an interview?

answer.text: A. Arrive early, research the company, practice answers.

feedback.text: This starts with a later step. Preparation should begin before the day of the interview.

answer.text: B. Practice answers, arrive early, research the company.

feedback.text: This puts research after practice. Strong practice depends on knowing the situation first.

answer.text: C. Arrive early, practice answers, research the company.

feedback.text: This order is confusing because arrival happens after preparation.

answer.text: D. Research the company, practice answers, arrive early.

feedback.text: Correct. The steps move from preparation to final action in a logical sequence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which outline shows a quality speech format?

answer.text: A. Introduction, Point 1, Point 2, Point 3, Conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. This structure helps the speaker and audience follow the presentation.

answer.text: B. Point 2, conclusion, random fact, introduction.

feedback.text: This order does not follow an accepted speech structure.

answer.text: C. A single paragraph with no clear parts.

feedback.text: This makes it hard to see the speech structure and weakens organization.

answer.text: D. A list of jokes before the topic is introduced.

feedback.text: This does not show a clear presentation format or coherent focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which sentence uses an appropriate voice and tone for an informative classroom speech?

answer.text: A. You all should already know this.

feedback.text: This sounds dismissive and can distance the audience.

answer.text: B. This topic is boring, but I have to present it.

feedback.text: This weakens the speaker's credibility and tone.

answer.text: C. Today I will explain three practical ways students can prepare for a presentation.

feedback.text: Correct. The tone is respectful, clear, and focused on informing the audience.

answer.text: D. I guess I will say some stuff now.

feedback.text: This is too casual and unclear for a formal classroom presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which main point best supports the focus "Public speaking practice improves confidence"?

answer.text: A. Rehearsing aloud helps speakers become more comfortable with their words.

feedback.text: Correct. This point directly supports how practice builds confidence.

answer.text: B. Some classrooms have desks in rows.

feedback.text: This does not connect to public speaking practice or confidence.

answer.text: C. Lunch schedules can affect student energy.

feedback.text: This shifts to a different topic and weakens focus.

answer.text: D. Many people enjoy watching movies.

feedback.text: This is unrelated to the speech focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Why are transitions important in a speech?

answer.text: A. They replace the need for main points.

feedback.text: Transitions do not replace content. They connect content.

answer.text: B. They help the audience understand how one idea leads to the next.

feedback.text: Correct. Transitions guide listeners through the speech structure.

answer.text: C. They let the speaker add unrelated information.

feedback.text: Transitions should strengthen focus, not introduce unrelated ideas.

answer.text: D. They make the conclusion unnecessary.

feedback.text: A conclusion is still needed to close the speech and restate the focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which plan is most coherent?

answer.text: A. Topic: school; points: clubs, weather, favorite songs.

feedback.text: These points do not support one clear focus.

answer.text: B. Topic: exercise; points: phones, homework, cafeteria food.

feedback.text: These ideas are unrelated to exercise.

answer.text: C. Topic: study groups; points: shared notes, peer support, regular review.

feedback.text: Correct. Each point supports the same topic and focus.

answer.text: D. Topic: attendance; points: sports teams, music apps, weekend plans.

feedback.text: These points drift away from attendance.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

A speaker labels each part of the outline and places transitions between main points. Which skill is the speaker showing?

answer.text: A. Avoiding all structure.

feedback.text: The speaker is using structure, not avoiding it.

answer.text: B. Replacing speaking with writing.

feedback.text: An outline supports speaking but does not replace delivery.

answer.text: C. Adding unrelated details.

feedback.text: Labels and transitions support organization when they connect ideas.

answer.text: D. Following a clear presentation format.

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker is using accepted speech parts to create quality work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

What should a speaker do first when organizing a speech?

answer.text: A. Choose random transitions.

feedback.text: Transitions work best after the speaker knows the focus and points.

answer.text: B. Decide the central focus of the speech.

feedback.text: Correct. The focus guides every later decision about points and order.

answer.text: C. Write the conclusion before knowing the topic.

feedback.text: A conclusion should match the speech focus and main points.

answer.text: D. Add as many facts as possible.

feedback.text: Facts need to be selected because they support the focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which transition uses a clear and respectful tone?

answer.text: A. Now that we have looked at the first reason, let us examine a second reason.

feedback.text: Correct. The tone is clear, respectful, and helps the audience follow.

answer.text: B. Whatever, here is another thing.

feedback.text: This is too casual and does not explain the connection.

answer.text: C. I am moving on because I am done with that.

feedback.text: This focuses on the speaker instead of guiding the audience.

answer.text: D. This part might not matter, but listen anyway.

feedback.text: This weakens the speaker's confidence and tone.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which conclusion best closes a speech about practicing presentations?

answer.text: A. That is all, and I also like science.

feedback.text: This adds an unrelated idea and does not close the focus.

answer.text: B. I forgot some of my points, but that is okay.

feedback.text: This does not reinforce the speech purpose.

answer.text: C. There are many topics I could have talked about.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not summarize the speech.

answer.text: D. Regular practice helps speakers prepare, manage nerves, and communicate clearly.

feedback.text: Correct. This conclusion restates the focus and summarizes the key points.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which main point does not fit the focus "Healthy routines can improve student learning"?

answer.text: A. Getting enough sleep helps students concentrate.

feedback.text: This supports the focus because sleep connects to learning.

answer.text: B. Some students prefer blue notebooks.

feedback.text: Correct. Notebook color does not explain how healthy routines improve learning.

answer.text: C. Eating breakfast can support energy in class.

feedback.text: This supports the focus because energy affects learning.

answer.text: D. Planning study time can reduce stress.

feedback.text: This supports the focus because planning is part of a healthy routine.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What does a preview statement usually do in a speech introduction?

answer.text: A. It ends the speech.

feedback.text: A preview appears near the beginning, not the end.

answer.text: B. It replaces all evidence.

feedback.text: A preview guides the audience but does not replace support.

answer.text: C. It tells the audience the main points the speech will cover.

feedback.text: Correct. A preview prepares listeners for the organization of the speech.

answer.text: D. It introduces an unrelated story.

feedback.text: An unrelated story can distract from the focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

A speaker says, "This information may help you prepare for your next class presentation." What does this show?

answer.text: A. Audience-aware tone.

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker connects the information to the audience in a respectful way.

answer.text: B. A loss of focus.

feedback.text: The sentence keeps the presentation connected to the audience and topic.

answer.text: C. An unrelated conclusion.

feedback.text: The sentence is relevant to the topic of presentation preparation.

answer.text: D. A missing main point.

feedback.text: The sentence may introduce or connect content; it is not automatically missing a point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which revision improves coherence?

answer.text: A. Add more unrelated examples to make the speech longer.

feedback.text: More unrelated material makes coherence weaker.

answer.text: B. Remove transitions so the speech sounds faster.

feedback.text: Removing transitions can make the speech harder to follow.

answer.text: C. Change the topic every time the audience seems interested.

feedback.text: Changing topics breaks focus.

answer.text: D. Remove the point about cafeteria food from a speech about joining clubs.

feedback.text: Correct. Removing an unrelated point helps every idea support the same focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speech plan uses problem-solution organization?

answer.text: A. First, I will describe three favorite apps.

feedback.text: This is a list, not a problem-solution structure.

answer.text: B. First, I will tell a joke, then another joke.

feedback.text: This does not identify a problem and solution.

answer.text: C. First, I will explain why students miss deadlines, then I will present ways to plan ahead.

feedback.text: Correct. The first part names the problem and the second part offers solutions.

answer.text: D. First, I will compare two unrelated school rules.

feedback.text: Comparison is different from problem-solution organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which item belongs in a speech outline?

answer.text: A. Private notes that are unrelated to the speech.

feedback.text: Unrelated private notes do not support the presentation format.

answer.text: B. Main points that support the speech focus.

feedback.text: Correct. Main points are core parts of an organized speech outline.

answer.text: C. Random words copied from a website.

feedback.text: Random copied words do not show quality speech planning.

answer.text: D. A conclusion that introduces a new topic.

feedback.text: A conclusion should close the same topic, not introduce a new one.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which introduction best prepares the audience for an organized speech?

answer.text: A. Today I will explain three ways planning ahead helps students manage homework.

feedback.text: Correct. It states the topic and previews the organized direction.

answer.text: B. I am going to talk for a while and see what happens.

feedback.text: This does not give a clear focus or structure.

answer.text: C. There are many things in school, and I will mention some.

feedback.text: This is vague and unfocused.

answer.text: D. My topic keeps changing, but I will begin anyway.

feedback.text: This signals weak organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which tone problem would most likely weaken a classroom presentation?

answer.text: A. Speaking clearly and respectfully.

feedback.text: This supports, rather than weakens, a classroom presentation.

answer.text: B. Explaining how the topic connects to students.

feedback.text: This shows audience awareness.

answer.text: C. Sounding dismissive toward the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. A dismissive tone can reduce audience trust and attention.

answer.text: D. Using transitions to guide listeners.

feedback.text: Transitions improve organization and listening.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which question helps test whether a speech is focused?

answer.text: A. Is the speech as long as possible?

feedback.text: Length does not prove focus. A long speech can still be disorganized.

answer.text: B. Does the speaker use complicated words?

feedback.text: Difficult vocabulary is not the same as coherent focus.

answer.text: C. Does the speech include every idea the speaker knows?

feedback.text: Including every idea can weaken focus.

answer.text: D. Does each main point support the same central idea?

feedback.text: Correct. This question checks whether the speech stays coherent.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What is the strongest reason to use an outline before speaking?

answer.text: A. It helps the speaker arrange ideas before presenting them.

feedback.text: Correct. An outline supports clear organization and delivery.

answer.text: B. It guarantees the audience will agree.

feedback.text: Organization helps understanding, but it does not guarantee agreement.

answer.text: C. It allows the speaker to ignore transitions.

feedback.text: A good outline often includes transitions.

answer.text: D. It replaces the need to understand the topic.

feedback.text: The speaker still needs to understand the topic and purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which pair of main points best supports the focus "Reading aloud improves speaking skills"?

answer.text: A. Reading aloud is useful; cafeterias sell snacks.

feedback.text: The second point is unrelated and weakens the focus.

answer.text: B. Reading aloud improves pronunciation; reading aloud builds confidence.

feedback.text: Correct. Both points directly support the focus.

answer.text: C. Reading aloud is loud; phones are popular.

feedback.text: The phone point does not support the focus.

answer.text: D. Reading aloud happens at home; math tests are difficult.

feedback.text: The math test point is unrelated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which phrase would best signal a final point in a speech?

answer.text: A. I forgot what comes next.

feedback.text: This weakens confidence and does not guide the audience.

answer.text: B. Anyway, one more thing.

feedback.text: This is casual and does not clearly organize the speech.

answer.text: C. Finally, the last reason practice matters is that it improves timing.

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase signals order and connects the final point to the focus.

answer.text: D. This next idea is random.

feedback.text: This tells the audience the speech is not coherent.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

A speaker's second point does not connect to the speech focus. What should the speaker do?

answer.text: A. Keep it because more points always improve a speech.

feedback.text: More points do not help if they are unrelated.

answer.text: B. Move it to the conclusion without changing it.

feedback.text: An unrelated idea will still weaken the conclusion.

answer.text: C. Say it faster so the audience notices less.

feedback.text: Speed does not solve a focus problem.

answer.text: D. Revise or replace it with a point that supports the focus.

feedback.text: Correct. Every main point should connect to the central idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which statement best describes coherent focus?

answer.text: A. All parts of the speech work together to support one clear idea.

feedback.text: Correct. Coherence means the audience can follow how every part connects.

answer.text: B. The speech includes as many topics as possible.

feedback.text: Too many topics can make the speech unfocused.

answer.text: C. The speaker never uses transitions.

feedback.text: Transitions often help create coherence.

answer.text: D. The conclusion introduces a new subject.

feedback.text: A conclusion should close the same focus, not shift topics.
